title: Which home energy upgrades will save you money? We did the math.
summary: A 2025 Washington Post model of a gas-heated Maryland house finds solar and a heat pump water heater pay back but a heat pump saves little against cheap gas.

assertions.quote: But installing it would cost around $12,000 after rebates, making the payback period around 48 years.
making the payback period around 48 years
the difference between the cost of a new heat pump and a new furnace — bringing the payback time closer to eight years
just 1 kWh of electricity can pull 3 or 4 kWh of heat indoors
In Maryland, electricity is about three times the cost of gas, sapping most of the benefits of switching to a heat pump.
“It’s a relationship between the outdoor temperature, your rates and the efficiency of the heat pump,”
if this home was subject to Chicago’s weather and prices of utilities, switching to a minimum efficiency heat pump could actually lose money
you are most likely to save money if you’re switching from an older, less efficient gas furnace

verdicts.note: A 70-80% AFUE furnace burns more gas per unit of heat than a new one, so the comparison favors the heat pump more.
In cold climates heat pumps save the median household $100-$200/yr less when replacing a 95% AFUE furnace rather than an 80% one.
Modeled cost savings were 40% replacing an 82% propane furnace versus 30% replacing a condensing propane furnace (metro), and 36% versus 26% in northern Minnesota.

assertions.quote: homeowners could save money switching from fuel oil, which is relatively expensive, but not from gas
“Unlike oil or gas systems, a heat pump becomes greener over time as the grid decarbonizes,”

verdicts.note: A heat pump's emissions track the grid's carbon intensity, which has been falling in most US regions.
As the grid becomes cleaner, electrification yields greater CO2 reductions; the model assumes grid emissions fall over the heat pump's life.
RMI expects the carbon benefit of heat pumps in California to grow as the grid moves toward 50% renewables by 2030, and expects Chicago's result to swing in favour as coal retires.
Edwards states that high heat pump use is likely to cut greenhouse gas emissions across much of the US, especially as the grid continues to decarbonize.
LBNL notes that electrification at comparable project cost locks in long-term carbon benefits as the grid becomes cleaner; this is stated reasoning, not a measured trend.

Using UK government grid forecasts, annual savings rise from 1.16 to 1.86 t CO2eq by 2043 as electricity decarbonises (68% lifetime cut); the rise is a projection that holds consumption fixed, not a measurement.

assertions.quote: Switching to a heat pump version, energy auditors found, would save $240 per year and cost just $978 after local utility rebates.
